config.title: Next.js App Router Fundamentals

intro.title: Next.js App Router Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page website using Next.js 13+ with its new App Router. You'll learn the core concept of file-based routing, where creating folders and files automatically defines the routes of your application. The main technologies involved are React components, TypeScript for type safety, and Next.js-specific features like the `page.tsx` file convention. By the end, you'll understand how to structure a basic Next.js app, navigate between pages, and use the App Router's layout system.
intro.usecase: The Next.js App Router is the foundation for building modern, performant web applications with features like server-side rendering and static generation. You'll use it to create e-commerce product pages that load instantly, marketing sites with optimized SEO, and dashboard applications with complex nested layouts. Real-world examples include Shopify storefronts with fast-loading product listings, Airbnb's property detail pages with image galleries, and admin panels like Vercel's dashboard with nested navigation. Mastering the App Router lets you build applications that feel snappy to users while maintaining clean, maintainable code architecture.

objectives: Apply the Next.js App Router to create a new Next.js 13+ project with TypeScript configuration
Construct page components using the file-system based routing convention in the app directory
Implement dynamic routes by creating folders with square bracket notation for parameterized URLs
Use the Link component from next/link to navigate between pages with client-side routing
Execute data fetching operations in server components using async/await with fetch API
Define layout components that persist across multiple pages with shared UI elements
Utilize the useRouter hook to access route parameters and query strings in client components
Implement loading and error UI by creating loading.tsx and error.tsx files in route segments
Apply metadata API to define page titles and descriptions for SEO optimization
Construct API routes by creating route handlers in the app/api directory structure
Use server actions to handle form submissions with server-side data mutations
Implement route groups to organize related routes without affecting the URL structure

steps.title: Initialize page state
steps.instruction: Inside your page component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'count' initialized to 0 with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.hint: Import useState from 'react' if you haven't already, then declare the state variable inside your component function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The page component now has a typed count state variable initialized to 0, ready to be used in subsequent steps.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized a typed count state variable with useState. The TypeScript annotation ensures type safety for this numeric state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've: 1) imported useState, 2) declared the count variable, 3) used TypeScript typing <number>, and 4) initialized it to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing state. You need to use the useState hook to create a count variable with TypeScript typing. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Define increment handler
steps.instruction: Inside your Page component, define a function named incrementCount that increases the count state by 1. The function should use the setCount state setter.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with the current count plus 1. You can use the previous state pattern: setCount(prev => prev + 1).
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an incrementCount function that properly updates the count state when called.
successCriteria: The code must include a function named incrementCount that calls setCount to increase count by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the incrementCount handler function. This function will be used later to update the count state when a button is clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there's an issue with your incrementCount function. Make sure it properly calls setCount to increase the count by 1. You can use either setCount(count + 1) or setCount(prev => prev + 1).
steps.feedbackWrong: The incrementCount function is not correctly defined. You need to create a function that increases the count state by 1 using the setCount state setter. Check that you're using the correct function name and properly updating the state.

steps.title: Add button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the main div. The button should have an onClick handler that calls incrementCount, a className of 'px-4 py-2 bg-blue-500 text-white rounded hover:bg-blue-600', and display text 'Increment Count'.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with onClick={incrementCount}. Remember to include the className and text content as specified.
